mainTopic: Payment for improving shared property, and how much a שומר may deduct for natural loss of stored produce, wine and oil
overview: This amud first finishes the story of מרי בר איסק, who improved the family estate without knowing he had a younger brother. רבה supports רב חסדא's ruling that the improvements are shared. אביי objects that מרי never knew about his brother, so he could not have given up payment for his work. רבי אמי argues from a captive's relatives, who are paid like an אריס. רב חסדא answers that those relatives had בית דין's permission, and that בית דין never appoints a relative over a קטן's property, so רבי אמי agrees. A new משנה then lists how much a שומר may deduct for natural loss of stored grain, with three opinions on how the deduction grows with the size of the pile. The גמרא explains the rates, limits them to mixed produce whose real loss cannot be measured, defines a large amount as ten כורין, and discusses grain that swells in the rainy season. A second משנה gives the deductions for wine and oil, and the גמרא explains that the sixth and the fifth reflect different local jugs. The amud ends with a story about how רב יהודה sold wine, and the next amud explains it.

steps.title: רבה agrees: the improvements go to the shared estate
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives the same ruling as רב חסדא: improvements made to an estate that was not yet divided are shared by all the heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise רבה said: whatever they improved goes to the middle, meaning it is shared equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבה, who supports רב חסדא's ruling against מרי בר איסק. רבה says that improvements made to the family estate are shared by all the brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן tells us רבה is lining up with the ruling just given, so מרי gets no extra payment for his work. The idea of השביחו לאמצע comes from the rule about brothers who improve their father's estate before it is divided: the profit is split, not given to the one who did the work.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; this view matches the one just said
To the middle, meaning shared by everyone

phrases.english: And likewise, Rabba said:
They improved it, so the gain goes to the middle.
phrases.notes: "The middle" means the shared pot, so all the brothers split the gain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's ruling from just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Improvements made to an undivided estate belong to all the heirs equally.

steps.title: אביי: the cases are not the same, because מרי did not know about his brother
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that brothers who grow up together knowingly give up payment for their work, but מרי did not know his brother existed, so he could not have given anything up.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are these really alike? There, the older brothers know about the younger ones and willingly give up payment. Here, did מרי know about his brother, so that he could give it up?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's ruling. He says the source it relies on does not fit מרי בר איסק's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Older brothers do not get paid for improvements because they know they are working for their younger siblings too, so we assume they forgive the payment. מרי thought the land was all his and had no idea he had a brother. You cannot forgive something you never knew about, so the reason for not paying him falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it similar? A standard way of rejecting a comparison
There (in the source case)... here (in our case)
They forgive, they give up what is owed to them

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not denying the rule that improvements are shared. He only says the rule depends on the older brothers knowingly giving up payment, and that is missing here.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Are they comparable?
There, the adults regarding the minors
know about them and give it up,
phrases.notes: They give up being paid for their work, since they know they are working for their younger brothers too.

phrases.english: here, did he know, so that he could give it up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's comparison in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between brothers who knowingly share an estate and מרי, who did not know his brother existed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not paying the worker rests on him forgiving the payment, and you cannot forgive without knowing.

steps.title: רבי אמי: if a captive's relatives get paid, surely מרי should be
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי argues with a קל וחומר: relatives who work a captive's land are paid like a sharecropper, even though none of it is theirs. מרי worked land that was partly his own, so he should certainly be paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter traveled and reached רבי אמי. He said to them: they taught something even bigger than this. We pay them like a sharecropper. Now, when it is his own property, we would not pay him?
steps.whatsHappening: The case reaches רבי אמי, who challenges רב חסדא's ruling. He uses a קל וחומר to argue that מרי should be paid for his work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that relatives who take care of a captive's property get paid for their work the way a sharecropper (אריס) does, even though the land is not theirs at all. מרי worked land that was at least partly his own. So he should surely get paid at least as much.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter rolled along, meaning the case got passed on
They taught something even stronger than this
We assess, we set a value
A sharecropper who works a field for a share of the crop

phrases.english: The matter rolled on
and came before Rabbi Ami.
He said to them: They said something greater than this:
We assess for them as for a sharecropper,
phrases.notes: "Them" means relatives who took over the land of someone taken captive.

phrases.english: now, for his own, we do not give him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רב חסדא's ruling, this time from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that מרי gets no payment for his improvements.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if someone working land that is not his gets paid, someone working land that is partly his should surely get paid.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the captive's relative had permission, מרי did not
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the קל וחומר. The captive's relative went onto the land with the בית דין's permission, while מרי went in on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought it back before רב חסדא. He said to them: Are these alike? There, he went in with permission. Here, he did not go in with permission.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא hears רבי אמי's argument and answers it. He shows that the captive's case is different from מרי's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The relative of a captive is sent by בית דין to manage the land, so he is paid for authorized work. מרי took over the land on his own, without anyone appointing him. Since the captive's case has a reason to pay that מרי's case lacks, the קל וחומר does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down, meaning went in to work the property

phrases.english: They brought this back before Rav Ḥisda.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets (הָא) and some leave it out. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: He said to them: Are they comparable?
There, he went in with permission,
here, he did not go in with permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם בִּרְשׁוּת נָחֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's קל וחומר from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the קל וחומר comparing the captive's relative to מרי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The captive's relative worked with בית דין's permission. מרי worked without it.

steps.title: רב חסדא's second point: בית דין never appoints a relative over a minor's property
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds that the brother was a קטן, and בית דין does not put a relative in charge of a minor's land. So מרי could never have had permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, he is a minor, and we do not send a relative onto a minor's property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a second, stronger reason. Because the brother was a minor, מרי could not have received permission even if he had asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer only said מרי happened to have no permission. This answer says permission was impossible, because בית דין does not let a relative manage a קטן's property. So the captive's case cannot apply to מרי at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; a second answer is coming
A minor, a child not yet of age
We do not send in, we do not appoint

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that בית דין does not appoint a relative to manage a minor's property, and that rule is what decides the case.

phrases.english: And furthermore: he is a minor,
phrases.notes: "He" is מרי's younger brother, who was a child when the estate was inherited.

phrases.english: and we do not send a relative down onto a minor's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second answer to רבי אמי's challenge.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully blocks the comparison to the captive's case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Permission was impossible here, because בית דין does not appoint a relative over a minor's property.

steps.title: רבי אמי agrees: he had not been told the brother was a minor
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי accepts רב חסדא's answer. He explains that nobody told him the brother was a minor, and that fact changes the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought it back before רבי אמי. He said to them: they did not finish telling me that he was a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is brought back to רבי אמי, and he gives in. His challenge came from not knowing all the facts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי does not argue with the rule that בית דין does not appoint a relative over a minor's property. He only says he did not know the brother was a קטן. So רב חסדא's ruling stands, and מרי gets no extra payment for his improvements.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not finish it, meaning they did not tell the whole story

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's ruling stands. A relative who works a captive's land is paid because בית דין sent him. מרי had no permission, and since his brother was a קטן he could not have gotten any, so he is not paid for his improvements.

phrases.english: They brought it back before Rabbi Ami,
he said to them: They did not finish it before me
that he is a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אמי accepts the answer given in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אמי withdraws his challenge, and רב חסדא's ruling that מרי is not paid for his improvements stands.

steps.title: The משנה's chart of how much produce shrinks in storage
steps.stepSummary: A שומר who returns stored produce may subtract a fixed amount for natural loss. The amount depends on the type of grain, the size of the pile, and how long it was stored.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone leaves produce with his friend, the friend may subtract the normal losses. For wheat and rice, he subtracts nine half-קבין per כור. For barley and millet, nine קבין per כור. For spelt and flaxseed, three סאין per כור. It all depends on the amount and on the time.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It lists how much a שומר is allowed to take off for the normal shrinking of stored grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stored grain dries out, gets eaten by mice, and some of it gets lost, so the שומר does not have to return the full original amount. Each grain gets its own rate: about 1/40 for wheat and rice, 1/20 for barley and millet, and 1/10 for spelt and flaxseed. The last line says the deduction grows with the size of the pile and with the time it was stored.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who leaves an item with another person to look after
Losses: the natural shrinking of stored produce
A large dry measure, equal to 30 סאין or 180 קבין
A small dry measure. Six קבין make one סאה
A medium dry measure. Thirty סאין make one כור

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who deposits produce with his friend
that friend deducts the losses for him
For wheat and for rice
nine half-kavs per kor
For barley and for millet
nine kavs per kor
For spelt and for flaxseed
three se'ahs per kor
Everything is according to the amount
and everything is according to the time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier story about מרי is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר of produce may subtract a fixed rate of loss for each type of grain. The rate is figured per כור and for the time stored.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: mice eat the same no matter the pile size
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues that the loss does not grow with a bigger pile, so the שומר subtracts for only one כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: Why should the mice care? They eat the same amount whether the pile is big or small! So the שומר subtracts losses for one כור only.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees with the תנא קמא's rule that the deduction grows with the amount stored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a question to make his point: mice eat what they eat, so a larger pile does not lose more. He keeps the per-grain rates but caps the deduction at the loss of one כור, however big the deposit is. He is arguing against "הכל לפי המדה" from the end of the תנא קמא's words.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it matter, or why should they care?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said
And what do the mice care?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא אוֹכְלוֹת בֵּין מֵהַרְבֵּה וּבֵין מִקִּמְעָה
phrases.english: Don't they eat the same, whether from a lot or from a little!
Rather, he does not deduct losses for him
except for one kor alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי וְכִי מָה אִכְפַּת לָהֶן לָעַכְבָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's rule that the deduction grows with the amount stored.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deduction is capped at the loss rate of one כור, whatever the size of the deposit.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a big pile has no deduction at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that if the deposit was large, the שומר subtracts nothing, because a large pile gains volume.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: If it was a large amount, he does not subtract losses, because large amounts grow.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the משנה. רבי יהודה says that for a large deposit there is no deduction at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says a bigger pile means a bigger deduction. רבי יוחנן בן נורי caps it at one כור. רבי יהודה goes furthest: a big pile swells, and that gain cancels out the loss, so the שומר returns the full amount.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views in the משנה. The תנא קמא says the deduction grows with the amount and the time. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says to deduct for one כור only. רבי יהודה says a large pile gets no deduction at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says
If it was a large amount
he does not deduct losses for him
because they increase.
phrases.notes: He means a big pile gains volume over time, and that makes up for what is lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אִם הָיְתָה מִדָּה מְרוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion that goes further than רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a large deposit there is no deduction, because the growth balances the loss.

steps.title: Rice loses more than the משנה says
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rate for rice. In real life, rice shrinks much more than nine half-קבין per כור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But rice loses a lot more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking how the משנה can give rice the same small loss rate as wheat, when rice actually loses much more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה put rice together with wheat at the lowest rate. The גמרא points out that this does not match what really happens to rice in storage. Something about the rice in the משנה needs to be explained.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rice loses a lot more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rice rate given in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rate of nine half-קבין per כור for rice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In real life rice shrinks much more than that, so the rate seems wrong.

steps.title: The משנה means shelled rice
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, answers that the משנה is talking about rice that was already shelled, which loses less.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The משנה was taught about shelled rice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about rice. The משנה means shelled rice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unshelled rice loses a lot because its husks fall away and it dries out. Shelled rice is already cleaned, so it loses only a little, like wheat. The משנה's low rate therefore makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught: the משנה was taught about this case

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said
They taught it about shelled rice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּאוֹרֶז קָלוּף שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about rice.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה is limited to one kind of rice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to mean all rice, which really loses much more.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means only shelled rice, which loses little.

steps.title: Flaxseed loses so much because it is on its stalks
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי חייא, explains that the high rate for flaxseed is about flaxseed still on its stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: For spelt and flaxseed, three סאין per כור, and so on. רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי חייא: The משנה was taught about flaxseed on its stalks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and explains why flaxseed has such a high loss rate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three סאין per כור is a large loss, a tenth of the pile. רבי חייא explains that the משנה means flaxseed stored while still on its stalks, which dry out and fall apart. Rice was explained by limiting it to the low-loss kind. Flaxseed is explained by limiting it to the high-loss kind.

phrases.english: For spelt and for flaxseed
three se'ahs per kor, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said that Rabbi Chiya said
They taught it about flaxseed on its stalks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא זֶרַע פִּשְׁתָּן בְּגִבְעוֹלִין שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a second rate in the משנה, the same way rice was explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The high rate for flaxseed applies to flaxseed stored on its stalks.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports both explanations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives three סאין per כור for flaxseed on its stalks and for unshelled rice. This backs up both רבי חייא and רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: for spelt, for flaxseed on its stalks, and for unshelled rice, the loss is three סאין per כור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says outright what the two אמוראים explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says "flaxseed on its stalks" in so many words, which matches רבי חייא. It also puts unshelled rice at the high rate of three סאין, which shows that the משנה's low rice rate must be about shelled rice.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: support from an outside source

phrases.english: It was also taught this way
For spelt and for flaxseed on its stalks
and for unshelled rice
three se'ahs per kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanations given for rice and for flaxseed.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's flaxseed means flaxseed on its stalks, and its rice means shelled rice
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists flaxseed on its stalks and unshelled rice at three סאין per כור

steps.title: The rate applies to every כור and every year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the end of the משנה. The fixed loss is counted again for each כור and for each year of storage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Everything is according to the amount, and so on. A ברייתא taught: This rate applies to each and every כור, and to each and every year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of the משנה and uses a ברייתא to explain what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "According to the amount" means you multiply the rate by the number of כורים stored. "According to the time" means you multiply it by the number of years stored. So two כורים of wheat kept for two years would lose four times the basic rate.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rates are counted per כור and per year. The rice rate is for shelled rice. The flaxseed rate is for flaxseed on its stalks.

phrases.english: Everything is according to the amount, etc.
It was taught
So too for each and every kor
and so too for each and every year.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל לְפִי הַמִּדָּה וְכוּ׳ תָּנָא כֵּן לְכׇל כּוֹר וָכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the last line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loss rate is counted separately for each כור and for each year of storage.

steps.title: The חכמים answer רבי יוחנן בן נורי: loss is not only from mice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that the חכמים answered רבי יוחנן בן נורי. Much produce gets lost and scattered, so the loss does grow with the amount stored.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said, and so on. A ברייתא teaches that the חכמים said to רבי יוחנן: A lot of the produce gets lost, and a lot of it gets scattered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which the חכמים push back against רבי יוחנן בן נורי's argument in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי argued that mice eat the same amount whether the pile is big or small, so the loss should not be counted again for each כור. The חכמים answer that mice are not the only cause of loss. Produce also gets lost and scattered, and that kind of loss grows with the size of the pile, so counting the loss per כור makes sense.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the חכמים count the loss again for each כור, against רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of his words in the משנה: what do the mice care whether there is a lot or a little?

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים, and this רבי יוחנן is רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.english: A lot of them get lost,
a lot of them get scattered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 14 said the loss is counted again for each כור. This step defends that rule against רבי יוחנן בן נורי's objection.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's argument that the loss does not depend on how much is stored.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Loss also comes from produce getting lost and scattered, and that grows with the amount stored.

steps.title: The fixed loss rates apply only when the produce was mixed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא limits the loss rates of the משנה to a case where the שומר mixed the owner's produce with his own. If he kept it in its own corner, he just returns it as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: When does this rule apply? When the שומר mixed the owner's produce with his own produce. But if he set aside a separate corner for it, he says to the owner: Here is yours in front of you.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא tells us exactly when the שומר subtracts the fixed loss amounts from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed rates are needed only when the owner's produce cannot be told apart from the שומר's own produce. If it was kept separately, there is nothing to calculate. Whatever is left in that corner is what the owner gets back.

keyTerms.meaning: Here is yours in front of you

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא does not say the loss is ignored when the produce was kept separate. The owner simply takes back whatever is actually left in that corner.

phrases.english: It was taught: In what case are these words said?
Where he mixed them with his own produce.
But if he set aside a corner for it,
he says to him: Here is yours in front of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows when the loss rates from Steps 10 to 14 are used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fixed loss rates apply only when the deposit was mixed with the שומר's own produce. If it was kept separately, he returns what is there.

steps.title: Even if it was mixed, why not just measure the real loss?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why mixing should matter. The שומר could check how much his own produce was and work out the real loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he mixed it with his own produce, what of it? Let him look at how much his own produce was!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: mixing does not seem to make the calculation impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שומר knows how much was his and how much was the owner's, he can measure the whole pile now. He can then split the real loss between the two of them according to their shares. So why would he need the fixed rates of the משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עֵירְבָן עִם פֵּירוֹתָיו מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: And if he mixed them with his own produce, what of it?
Let him look at how much his own was!
phrases.notes: He means: knowing both amounts, measure the whole pile and split the real loss fairly between the two shares.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי עֵירְבָן עִם פֵּירוֹתָיו מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case described in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that mixing makes the fixed loss rates necessary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The real loss can be measured and divided by each person's share, so there is no need to estimate it.

steps.title: He was taking from the mixed pile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שומר was taking produce from the mixed pile. That makes it impossible to measure the real loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he was taking supplies from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 17 by adding a detail to the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שומר kept taking produce from the pile for his own use, the pile shrank for two reasons: natural loss and his own use. Measuring the pile now cannot show how much was natural loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes supplies from, uses some of

phrases.english: Where he takes supplies from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a detail to the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mixed pile was left alone, so the real loss could be measured.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שומר took from the pile, so the real loss cannot be measured.

steps.title: Then let him figure out how much he took
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes again: the שומר could add back what he took and still work out the real loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him look at how much he took!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking from the pile is only a problem if the amount he took is unknown. If he knows how much he took, he can add it back and still find the real natural loss.

phrases.english: Then let him look at how much he took!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that taking from the pile makes the calculation impossible.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he knows how much he took, he can still calculate the real loss.

steps.title: He doesn't know how much he took
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שומר does not know how much he took. So the only way to figure the loss is with the fixed rates of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where they do not know how much he took.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer and completes the picture of when the משנה's loss rates are used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is fully defined. The produce was mixed, the שומר took from it, and nobody knows how much he took. Only then is there no way to measure the real loss, so the fixed amounts of the משנה are used.
steps.whatToRemember: The fixed loss rates of the משנה are used only when the real loss cannot be measured. That happens when the deposit was mixed with the שומר's own produce and he took an unknown amount from it. If the deposit was kept separate, the owner simply takes back what is there.

phrases.english: Where they do not know how much he took.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 and ends the discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a detail to the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The amount he took was known, so the real loss could be calculated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The amount he took is unknown, so the fixed rates of the משנה must be used.

steps.title: How much counts as a large amount?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the view of רבי יהודה in the משנה and asks how big a 'large amount' is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if it was a large amount, and so on. How much is a large amount?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי יהודה, who says that a large deposit gets no loss deduction. It is setting up a question about how big 'large' really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gave a rule without a number. Before anyone can apply it, we need to know where 'large' starts.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on: the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If it was, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The full line is: if the deposit was a large amount, he does not deduct for loss.

phrases.english: How much is a large amount?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of mixed produce and goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum size of a deposit that counts as a 'large amount' for רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A large amount is ten כורין
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, says a large amount is ten כורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: ten כורין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a number: ten כורין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives רבי יהודה's rule a clear line. A deposit of ten כורין or more gets no deduction for loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Kors, a large unit of volume for grain

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Ten kor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A large amount means ten כורין.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also defines a large amount as ten כורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: How much is a large amount? Ten כורין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תנאי source now backs up the answer of רבי יוחנן. Ten כורין stands as the accepted measure.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, introducing a ברייתא that supports what was just said

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, a 'large amount' is ten כורין. A ברייתא says the same.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
How much is a large amount?
Ten kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 22 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a large amount means ten כורין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the same number.

steps.title: A ברייתא limits the loss deduction
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites before רב נחמן that the loss deduction applies only when the grain was given and returned 'from the threshing floor.' If it was returned 'from the house,' there is no deduction because the grain increases.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב נחמן: When does this rule apply? When the owner measured it for him from his threshing floor and he returned it from his threshing floor. But if he measured it from his threshing floor and returned it from his house, he does not deduct the losses, because they increase.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא is recited that limits when the שומר may deduct for loss. Some cases get no deduction at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reading is that threshing-floor measures and house measures are different sizes. When the deposit is measured one way and returned the other way, the difference makes up for the loss. So the שומר deducts nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter who memorized and recited משניות and ברייתות
Losses: the natural shrinkage of the produce
They increase, they come out more

phrases.english: The tanna taught before Rav Nachman:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: "These words" means the rule that the שומר takes off a set amount for loss.

phrases.english: Where he measured it for him from his threshing floor
and returned it to him from his threshing floor.
But if he measured it for him from his threshing floor
and returned it to him from his house,
he does not deduct losses for him,
because they increase.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that limits when the משנה's loss deduction (step 7) applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loss deduction applies when the grain was given and returned the same way ('from the threshing floor'). If it was returned 'from the house,' there is no deduction because the grain 'increases.'

steps.title: No one uses two different measures
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects: people are not foolish enough to give with a big measure and take back with a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are we dealing with fools, who give with a big measure and take back with a small measure?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks the plain reading of the ברייתא. He says it makes no sense for an owner to deposit with one measure and take back with another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading of 'threshing floor versus house' depends on two different measures being used. רב נחמן says no sensible owner would deposit with a large measure and accept his grain back with a smaller one. So the ברייתא cannot mean that.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב נחמן, answering the תנא.

phrases.english: And are we dealing with fools
who give with a big measure
and take back with a small measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain reading of the ברייתא in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא means a threshing-floor measure versus a house measure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sensible owner would never deposit with one measure and take back with a smaller one. So the case as read is not realistic.

steps.title: It means threshing season versus rainy season
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rereads the ברייתא as talking about seasons. Grain given in the threshing season and returned in the rainy season swells, so there is no deduction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you mean 'in the days of the threshing floor.' When does this rule apply? When he measured it in the threshing season and returned it in the threshing season. But if he measured it in the threshing season and returned it in the rainy season, he does not deduct the loss, because the grain increases.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a new reading. The ברייתא is about time of year, not about different measuring vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, 'threshing floor' means the dry harvest season. Grain returned in the rainy season soaks up moisture and swells. The swelling makes up for the loss, so the שומר deducts nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: In the threshing season, the dry harvest time

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'מותירות' stay the same, but their meaning changes. They no longer mean the measure was bigger. They now mean the grain itself swelled from moisture.

phrases.english: Perhaps you are saying 'in the days of the threshing floor.'
In what case are these words said?
Where he measured it for him in the threshing season
and returned it to him in the threshing season.
But if he measured it for him in the threshing season
and returned it to him in the rainy season,
he does not deduct the loss for him
because they increase.
phrases.notes: Here this means the grain soaks up the damp air and swells.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 25 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about a threshing-floor measure versus a house measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the threshing season versus the rainy season, when the grain swells from moisture.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a real-world reason the שומר may owe the full amount back: the season changes the volume of the grain.

steps.title: Then the jug should burst
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: if the grain swells in the rainy season, the jug holding it should burst.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, the jug should burst!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the swelling explanation of step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If grain really grows in the rainy season, a jug filled to the top would have no room for it. The jug would crack. Since that does not normally happen, the swelling idea looks doubtful.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
If so, the jug should burst!
phrases.notes: "If so" means: if grain swells in the rainy season, as step 26 said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the swelling explanation of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that grain swells in the rainy season.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Swelling grain in a full jug should break the jug, and jugs do not normally break.

steps.title: It really happened: a jug burst
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there was a real case in which the jug did burst.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident, and the jug burst.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב פפא's point and says it really happens: a jug once burst.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of denying the problem, the answer agrees that the jug can burst. A real incident proves the grain truly swells, so the explanation of step 26 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real case that happened

phrases.english: There was an incident, and the jug burst.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by agreeing with it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge as true and supporting it with a real case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Jugs never burst, so grain cannot swell.
steps.terutzMaskana: Jugs did burst in a real case, so the grain really swells.

steps.title: Or: the grain presses together
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the jug need not burst, because the grain packs and presses together.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: it is because of the pressing together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to רב פפא. It explains the jug through the grain pressing together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not rely on jugs bursting. The grain inside presses and packs tightly, so the jug need not crack. This answers רב פפא's objection in a different way from step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another answer

steps.whatToRemember: A שומר does not deduct for loss when the grain was deposited in the threshing season and returned in the rainy season. Grain changes volume with the seasons.

phrases.english: If you want, say: because of the pressing together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 27, separate from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer through a physical explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Swelling grain must break the jug.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grain presses together tightly, so the jug need not burst.

steps.title: Deduction for wine: a sixth or a fifth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a שומר returning wine may deduct one-sixth for natural loss. רבי יהודה says one-fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He deducts one-sixth for wine. רבי יהודה says: one-fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It tells us how much wine a שומר may subtract when he gives back wine that was deposited with him, because some is lost naturally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine soaks into the walls of the jug and some is lost while it is stored, so the owner cannot expect the full amount back. The תנא קמא sets the loss at a sixth, and רבי יהודה sets it higher, at a fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: He deducts for him (subtracts from what he returns)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
He deducts for him one-sixth for wine.
Rabbi Yehuda says: one-fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about fixed deductions for loss in deposited liquids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר returning wine deducts a sixth (תנא קמא) or a fifth (רבי יהודה) for natural loss.

steps.title: Deduction for oil: three לוגין per hundred
steps.stepSummary: For oil, the שומר deducts three לוגין out of every hundred: one and a half for שמרים and one and a half for what soaks into the jug.
steps.simpleTranslation: He deducts three לוגין of oil for every hundred: a לוג and a half for sediment, and a לוג and a half for what is absorbed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the deduction for oil, and it explains exactly where the loss comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three לוגין are split into two causes. Part of the oil settles at the bottom as שמרים, and part soaks into the walls of the jug as בלע. Spelling out the two causes prepares for the next line, where each cause can be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Sediment that sinks to the bottom
Absorption into the walls of the jug

phrases.english: He deducts for him three log
of oil for a hundred:
a log and a half of sediment,
a log and a half absorbed.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹצִיא לוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה לוּגִּין שֶׁמֶן לְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wine to oil and gives a detailed breakdown of the loss.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For oil, deduct three לוגין per hundred: one and a half for שמרים and one and a half for בלע.

steps.title: When the oil deductions do not apply
steps.stepSummary: If the oil was refined, there is no deduction for שמרים. If the jugs were old, there is no deduction for בלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was refined oil, he does not deduct for sediment. If the jugs were old, he does not deduct for absorption.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two exceptions. Each one cancels one of the two causes of loss it just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Refined oil has already been cleaned, so no sediment will form. Old jugs have already soaked up all they can, so they will not absorb more. Each deduction applies only when its cause is really present.

keyTerms.meaning: Old jugs that have already absorbed liquid

phrases.english: If it was refined oil,
he does not deduct for him sediment.
If the jugs were old,
he does not deduct for him absorption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה שֶׁמֶן מְזוּקָּק אֵינוֹ יוֹצִיא לוֹ שְׁמָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the two oil deductions from the previous line to cases where their causes exist.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No deduction for שמרים with refined oil, and no deduction for בלע with old jugs.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even a buyer of refined oil accepts a sediment deduction
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that even someone who buys refined oil accepts a loss of a לוג and a half of שמרים per hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even one who sells refined oil to another all year round, the buyer accepts upon himself a לוג and a half of sediment for every hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a ruling about buying and selling. Even when oil is sold as refined, the buyer accepts that some of it will be sediment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous line said refined oil has no sediment deduction for a שומר. רבי יהודה says that in a sale, even refined oil is understood to include the standard amount of sediment, so the buyer cannot complain about it.

keyTerms.meaning: All the days of the year

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even one who sells refined oil to his fellow
all the days of the year,
this one accepts upon himself
a log and a half of sediment for a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אַף הַמּוֹכֵר שֶׁמֶן מְזוּקָּק לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related rule for a sale of refined oil, right after the refined-oil exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer of refined oil accepts a לוג and a half of שמרים per hundred.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's deductions follow the real causes of loss: sediment and absorption for oil, and a sixth or a fifth for wine.

steps.title: No real argument: each Sage followed his own region's jugs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה do not disagree about wine. Where one lived, jugs were coated with wax and absorbed little. Where the other lived, jugs were coated with pitch and absorbed a lot.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They do not disagree. Each Sage ruled according to his own place. In one Sage's place they coat jugs with wax, and it does not absorb much. In the other Sage's place they coat jugs with pitch, and it absorbs much.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the gap between a sixth and a fifth for wine. It is not a legal argument; each Sage was describing how much wine was lost in his own area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deduction is meant to match real loss, and real loss depends on how jugs are made. With a wax coating less wine soaks in, which gives a sixth. With a pitch coating more soaks in, which gives a fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: This Sage according to his place

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה have two different laws here. They agree on the principle; they only describe different local jugs.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And they do not disagree:

phrases.aramaic: מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ.
phrases.english: This Sage according to his place, and that Sage according to his place.
In the place of one Sage they coat with wax
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who said a sixth.

phrases.english: and it does not absorb much;
in the place of the other Sage they coat with pitch
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, who said a fifth.

phrases.english: and it absorbs much.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי מָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ וּמָר כִּי אַתְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the wine argument in step 30 and explains it as a difference in local conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sixth and the fifth reflect different local jug coatings, not different laws.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that these fixed deductions are estimates of real loss, so they can change from place to place.

steps.title: Another explanation: different kinds of clay
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the difference comes from the clay the jugs are made of: one kind absorbs more and another absorbs less.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because of the clay: this kind absorbs much and that kind does not absorb much.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second reason why the two Sages gave different numbers. This time the cause is the clay of the jug, not its coating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main idea stays the same: there is no real argument, only different local conditions. Only the cause changes, from the coating to the earth the jugs are made from.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another explanation)
Clay or earth used to make jugs

phrases.english: If you want, say: because of the clay,
this one absorbs much
and that one does not absorb much.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason for the same conclusion that the Sages do not disagree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation of the local difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference in absorption comes from the coating of the jugs.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can also come from the type of clay the jugs are made from.
steps.whatToRemember: The sixth and the fifth are not a real argument. Local jugs, whether because of their coating or their clay, absorb different amounts.

steps.title: How wine was sold in רב יהודה's town
steps.stepSummary: In רב יהודה's town a barrel held forty-eight pitchers and cost six זוזים. רב יהודה sold the wine at six pitchers per זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רב יהודה's place they would put forty-eight pitchers into a barrel. A barrel sold for six זוזים, and רב יהודה sold it at six pitchers for each זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about real prices and measures in רב יהודה's town. This sets up the next lines, where the numbers will be explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty-eight pitchers for six זוזים comes to eight pitchers per זוז, yet רב יהודה sold only six per זוז. The story stops here, and the גמרא will explain this gap next.

phrases.english: In Rav Yehuda's place

phrases.aramaic: פָּרֵיס רַב יְהוּדָה שִׁיתָּא שִׁיתָּא בְּזוּזָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda would sell six by six for a zuz,
phrases.notes: Literally "divided": he sold the barrel in small amounts, six pitchers for each זוז.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב יהודה's town a 48-pitcher barrel cost six זוזים, and he sold the wine at six pitchers per זוז.
